top.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
top.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday carried out the first-ever recovery of a spaceship, pulling off a successful “catch” of its Starship vessel as it returned to its launch site after a day in orbit. The spaceship emerged from a cloudy sky after withstanding the extreme heat of re-entering the Earth’s atmosphere, and descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The feat marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems — a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of space flight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into cheers as the spaceship eased into its high-tech nest on the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. This time the Starship spacecraft that gives the rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink satellite internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was extraordinarily complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters do. Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he added. ‘Giant swoosh’ The vessel’s path home was carefully mapped out by engineers. “If you want to get back to the east coast of Texas, you have to fly over the entire continent to get back there. So inevitably, you’re flying over land and we spend a lot of time figuring out the safest way to do that,” senior SpaceX engineer Lars Blackmore said. Starship flew over sparsely inhabited desert areas, wove over towns and then carried out a “giant swoosh maneuver” in its final approach, looping around the cities of Texas’ Rio Grande Valley and approaching its landing site from the east. Some versions of Starship are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while other iterations will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars. US space agency NASA is expecting Starship to serve as a lunar lander on its Artemis mission. On Saturday, Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated Musk and SpaceX. “It was almost magic… Making more believers by the day… one step closer to (the Moon),” he said on X. top.title: Arsène Wenger not expected to stand for FIFA presidency
top.description: FILE PHOTO - FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development Arsene Wenger stands in the stadium prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League final soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid at Wembley Stadium. (is associated with: «Arsène Wenger not expected to stand for FIFA presidency») Robert Michael/dpa Arsène Wenger has decided against standing for the FIFA presidency in a boost for current incumbent Gianni Infantino, the Press Association understands. Wenger was touted as a potential rival to Infantino, who has lost the confidence of European football’s governing body, UEFA, over the controversial plan to seek private investment in a World Cup company. The deadline for candidates to declare their intention to stand is Wednesday, November 18, but former Arsenal manager Wenger has informed UEFA he will not go head-to-head with Infantino, the Press Association understands. It was first stated by UEFA in August that work to identify a credible candidate to challenge Infantino had got under way and Wenger was encouraged to stand. A senior figure in European football told the Press Association they believe Wenger would be the only person who could beat Infantino and put football first. Even though Wenger is European, he has served as FIFA’s chief of global football development since 2019 and has the respect of the football world after his Premier League success, which was preceded by successful stints in his homeland of France and Japan. Wenger had also earned a strong command of respect in Africa for his development work within FIFA but, in a blow to UEFA, the 77-year-old will not stand. This move could cement Infantino’s position as president despite the fallout of plans to create a company titled FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would manage commercial interests of FIFA’s competitions including the men’s and women’s World Cups. A private investor group, led by a company founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, were proposed to hold a minority stake in FFE. However, Infantino had to abandon the plan days after it emerged publicly after it was rejected by UEFA along with the Asian confederation and CONCACAF. It is the latest controversy regarding Infantino, who faced scrutiny after FIFA’s disciplinary committee decided to suspend a ban imposed on US forward Folarin Balogun during this year's tournament. Trump later admitted he had personally called Infantino to review Balogun’s suspension, but FIFA’s president has of late consolidated support as he targets a fourth term in position and Wenger’s decision to not stand is welcome news for the 56-year-old ahead of the FIFA Congress next March. Infantino has pledged “unanimous” backing from the Confederation of African Football (CAF), while the Asian confederation has U-turned and will now support his presidency bid.

top.title: Why Marist football struggled in shut out by visiting Butler
top.description: Marist struggled to move the ball consistently and turned it over twice as the Red Foxes slipped out of any contention for the Pioneer Football League title with a 28-0 loss to Butler before 2,167 at Tenney Stadium in Poughkeepsie on Saturday, Nov. 14. Marist has dropped three of its past four, falling to 5-6 and 4-3 in the PFL. Butler (9-2) moved into a first-place tie with Dayton at 6-1. Butler has beaten Marist four consecutive times since 2021 and leads the all-time series 5-4. Butler is a physical team that lived up to its reputation for sturdy defense. The Red Foxes were 2-for-15 on third-down conversions and 1-for-5 on fourth down, leading to seven punts by Ethan Yuska (37.7 yards average). Quarterback Sonny Mannino (18-for-32, 138 yards) was picked off in the second quarter, after moving the ball down to the Butler 13, and again in the fourth. Mannino was also sacked six times, for 34 total yards. Butler got touchdown runs of 6 and 3 yards from Michael Dellumo in the second and third quarters, respectively, for a 14-0 lead - it was the second week in a row that Dellumo had a pair of scores. The second score was set up with a rare quick kick on third down, pushing Marist back to its own 2, and after stopping the Red Foxes on three plays Butler's Madden Beriault returned a punt to the 13. Gabe Passini capped an 11-play, 56-yard drive with a 1-yard TD run early in the fourth, and Desmin Jackson scored from 6 yards out 92 seconds later after Tristan Johnson picked off Mannino and returned it 42 yards. Marist was held to 52 total yards rushing and 141 passing. Isaiah Simmons had 10 carries for 36 yards. Lincoln Cardillo had five receptions for 32 yards, Reed Shumpert three for 48 and Zach Garmont three for 25. Kade Werner had nine tackles. Passini was 10-for-16 for 101 yards, adding 14 carries for 69 yards. Michael Dellumo had 12 carries for 46 and Desmin Jackson eight for 26. Jayden Norris had 2.5 sacks, Jackson Stratton had eight tackles and Andrew Lieske had the early interception for the Bulldogs. Butler has held eight foes under 87 yards rushing. Marist had scored in 13 consecutive games. The last time the Red Foxes were shut out was Nov. 1, 2025, at Saint Thomas (Minn.) by a 45-0 count. Butler shut out Franklin 52-0 on Sept. 12. Marist closes the season on Nov. 21 at Davidson. Butler will host Morehead State. Kickoff for both games is 1 p.m. Before the game, Marist honored 21 senior athletes and two managers. kmcmillan@th-record.com X / Twitter: @KenMcMillanTHR This article originally appeared on Times Herald-Record: Why Marist football struggled in shut out by visiting Butler

After thumping Argentina last week, Ireland failed to click in an unconvincing opening, with Tommy O'Brien's early try and a Robert Baloucoune double enough for a 17-15 lead. Fiji arrived in Dublin without a win in nine previous meetings against their hosts, and having been thrashed 54-17 by France last week. But they dreamed of a historic win after tries from Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato, and a Ben Volavola penalty, kept them firmly in the contest at the break. However, Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter and O'Brien crossed as Andy Farrell's men scored 26 unanswered second-half points to deny the Pacific Islanders, who remain without a point in the competition. The result left Ireland one point off northern hemisphere leaders France before next week's mouthwatering tussle with world champions South Africa in Dublin. When these sides last met, in Dublin two years ago, Ireland scored four converted tries to effectively end the contest by half-time on their way to a 52-17 win. But this was anything but simple. Despite making seven changes from last week's victory over the Pumas and losing centre Jamie Osborne to an early injury, Ireland threatened to gallop into the distance in a hurry. top.title: Michigan Football 4-star defensive commit flips to elite SEC program
top.description: Zach Libby/Maize n Brew It’s just about that time of year. No, I’m not taking about the holiday season or when my seasonal depression kicks in — I’m talking about #FlipSZN on the recruiting trail. Unfortunately, today’s update doesn’t favor the Wolverines, as 2027 four-star defensive back Tavares Harrington has flipped his commitment from Michigan to Ole Miss. I can only imagine he saw the Wolverines’ defense give up nearly 300 passing yards to Oregon quarterback Dylan Raiola and said, “Yeah, I’m good, fam.” BREAKING: Four-Star Safety Tavares Harrington has Flipped his Commitment from Michigan to Ole Miss, he tells me for @Rivals The 6’3 185 S had been Committed to the Wolverines since May “Shark business🦈🏡” https://t.co/C2BqkK3Z9D pic.twitter.com/KQMM6ZJTmj — Hayes Fawcett (@Hayesfawcett3) November 14, 2026 The 6-foot-3, 180-pound Chicago, Illinois native committed to Michigan back in May, following a visit for Michigan’s spring game. However, he took a visit to Ole Miss — one of the original runner-ups in his recruitment — the weekend of Nov. 7. Harrington was one of the early building blocks of Michigan’s 2027 class. He is ranked No. 151 overall, No. 9 at the safety position and No. 8 in Illinois on the Rivals Industry Rankings. He is a versatile prospect who was recruited to Michigan as a nickel/safety. The timing of all this is not great for Michigan, with the early signing period getting underway very soon. The program is kind of in disarray right now, too, as the Wolverines are coming off a 15-6 loss to Michigan State, offensive coordinator Jason Beck was fired, the team is (as of this writing) getting its ass kicked by Oregon, and there is plenty of uncertainty about the direction of the program. Harrington’s decision comes during a stretch when commits across the country are re-evaluating their options, and Michigan’s current struggles on the field make it harder to hang on to every pledge. Harrington’s departure leaves a hole in a secondary class that had been one of the strongest parts of Michigan’s 2027 haul. The Wolverines still hold commitments from four-star cornerbacks Blake Jenkins and Darius Johnson, as well as three-star legacy safety prospect Charles Woodson Jr. But losing a four-star recruit that the coaching staff prioritized from the very beginning of their time in Ann Arbor takes the class down a notch. There is also a Mount Carmel angle to monitor. Harrington comes from the same Chicago program as 2027 four-star wide receiver Quentin Burrell, who is still committed to Michigan. Will this affect what Burrell does during the early signing period? Considering Burrell committed before Harrington, it likely won’t have a major impact, but only time will tell. The bigger concern is whether this is the start of a trend. The early signing period opens Dec. 2, and Michigan has an offensive coordinator vacancy, an uncertain head coaching situation to some outside observers, and a lot of recruiting momentum to protect. top.title: White has 'exciting future' despite boos - Rice
top.description: Declan Rice joined Ben White at Arsenal after signing from West Ham in 2023 [Getty Images] Declan Rice has defended Arsenal team-mate Ben White after the defender was booed at Wembley during England's 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday. White, who came on as a substitute in the Nations League fixture, left the Three Lions' camp at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar to return home for personal reasons. He then made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Gareth Southgate's reign. White was also booed by some fans in March's 1-1 draw with Ukraine after returning to the squad under Thomas Tuchel. "The incident with Ben was over five years ago, I don't know why it is still a conversation to be honest," Rice told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Knowing Ben, knowing the character he is, he has totally moved on from all of that. "He always wears the shirt with pride and every time he puts on the shirt, he gives 100 percent. "It shows his character. It is not easy being booed coming on at Wembley, but to show his mental strength to play the game and to play well, like he did in the previous months, is a real testament to him." Rice also said that the players do not discuss the situation at all and that everybody has moved on, adding that White has "an exciting future ahead with this England squad". Before the game, White said that people did not know the "full story" behind his departure from Qatar but that he still backed his decision. Rice close to signing new Arsenal contract Rice has also confirmed that he is close to signing a new contract with Arsenal. BBC Sport first revealed the midfielder was set to sign a new long-term deal at Emirates Stadium on 7 October, and the 27-year-old, speaking before England's game against Spain on Sunday, said: "A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon and I'm extremely lucky to be at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust and team-mates who put so much energy in to me." Rice's current deal expires in 2028 but the former West Ham star is now expected to extended his tenure in north London, having arrived from London Stadium in 2023 in a deal worth £105m. The midfielder's new contract will put him alongside Bukayo Saka as Arsenal's top earner. Rice has managed to avoid upheaval during his career and he believes that continuity has helped him to blossom. "I've been extremely lucky I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career. I always set myself targets, pushing for more," he said. top.title: How did Minnesota survive travel adventure to Penn State football?
top.description: STATE COLLEGE — This became a Penn State football day like no other. At least for visiting Minnesota Golden Gophers . How will the Gophers and Nittany Lions handle their travel and injury issues for their season-turning Big Ten game on Saturday, Nov. 14, in Beaver Stadium? Penn State will miss its star receiver Koby Howard for the seventh straight game to an undisclosed injury. He'll also be joined on the sideline by key backups, defensive end Caleb Bacon and cornerback Jahmir Joseph, both also listed as "out" on the Big Ten's pregame availability report . Nittany Lion starting left tackle Malachi Goodman and backup safety Jeremiah Cooper were listed as "game-time decisions" on the report. Minnesota was even a tougher personnel position: They are missing nine players for Saturday's game, including eight with starting experience. Of course, they're also dealing with an unprecedented travel adventure. Minnesota was one of the few in the Big Ten that got caught in the midst of Friday's four-hour nationwide travel ground stop by the Federal Aviation Authority. Their flight was canceled after the team had boarded in the afternoon. The Gophers, inexplicably, traveled back to campus and could not fly to State College until Saturday morning. They arrived barely seven hours before kickoff. Minnesota arrived carrying a lot of baggage even beyond their unusual same-day arrival. The Gophers and Penn State are both 5-4 but appear to be trending in different directions. While the Nittany Lions broke a four-game losing streak with back-to-back victories, the Gophers are coming off consecutive, excruciating defeats to top-five Indiana and UCLA − games they were tied or led in the fourth quarter. Minnesota owns one of the worst-rated offenses in the nation. They also are now missing their pair of starting defensive tackles, Riley Sunram and Theorin Randle and may be without standout defensive back John Nestor. Penn State's list of unavailable players for the Minnesota game includes Howard, Joseph, Bacon, linebacker Alex Tatsch, defensive ends Max Granville , offensive lineman Will Thompkins, cornerback Tyler Armstead and defensive tackle Alijah Carnell. top.title: How Phoenix Suns plan to defend early MVP candidate Luka Doncic
top.description: The Phoenix Suns are very aware of Luka Doncic's red-hot start to this season. “He’s on a tear,” Suns forward Ryan Dunn said. Leading the league in scoring, Doncic is averaging a career-high 38.6 points a game in leading the Los Angeles Lakers (11-2) to the NBA’s best record. The Suns (5-6) are the next team with the daunting task of slowing down the early MVP candidate in the 2 p.m. game Sunday, Nov. 15, at Mortgage Matchup Center to end a season-long, seven-game homestand. “Limit the free throw line as much as you can,” Dunn continued. “Limit his 3s as much as we can. He's going to get to it regardless. He's not going to have a 0-point night. I'm not going to say it but hopefully keep it to a low-scoring game. I'm not going to say what we want to keep him to but just trying to make it tough for him as much as we can. "Don’t try to worry about making home run plays against him, because that's who he is. He's going to be able to dissect and operate the offense. Making it tough and individually just trying to do what I'm supposed to do, and collectively, just make it tough for him." Doncic is averaging an insane 41.8 points, 8.1 rebounds and 7.6 assists in six games during the Lakers’ current seven-game winning streak. He missed their road win against the Detroit Pistons with low back tightness. The Lakers landed Doncic in a shocking trade before the 2025 trade deadline. This marks his third season with the Lakers, but first without LeBron James, who is now with the Philadelphia 76ers. This is now Doncic’s team. “I do think the shift and his role and responsibility, even with some of the roster changes,” Suns coach Jordan Ott said. “Not that he has a ball in his hands more, but he's just a little bit into a place where it is his ball." top.title: Dodgers All-Star Free Agent Commanding Widespread Interest
top.description: Los Angeles Dodgers free agent Kris Bubic is gathering plenty of interest across MLB, per Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. The Dodgers acquired Bubic at the trade deadline on a rental, sending minor league reliever Carlos Duran the other way. “Free-agent left-hander Kris Bubic, who was traded from the Kansas City Royals to the Los Angeles Dodgers during his second stint on the injured list with elbow soreness, is drawing broad interest from contenders and non-contenders alike, according to a person briefed on his market,” Sammon and Rosenthal wrote. How Did Kris Bubic Perform With the Dodgers? Bubic came to the Dodgers on the injured list after struggling with elbow soreness, so he made just seven appearances out of the bullpen with the team throughout the regular season and postseason. Five of those appearances came in the regular season, where he held opponents scoreless through 4.2 innings pitched while striking out five batters. Bubic didn’t find the same success in the postseason, though, as he allowed two runs through 1.1 innings pitched. Sep 23, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers relief pitcher Kris Bubic (40) delivers against the San Diego Padres in the seventh inning at Dodger Stadium . Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Why is Kris Bubic Such a Popular Free Agent? Bubic, 29, is a starting pitcher by trade, but stepped into the bullpen for the Dodgers to manage his load after his injury. He has a versatile five-pitch arsenal, and he has a solid track record over the past few years despite a few injuries. Before an injury took him out of commission in July 2025, he had a 2.55 ERA through 20 starts and made the All-Star Game. This season, Bubic had a 3.76 mark through 14 appearances. Free agency is loaded with pitchers this offseason, with Tarik Skubal headlining a class which also consists of players like Freddy Peralta, Nick Martinez and Sonny Gray, but he is one of the top left-handed options available, and is one of the few still yet to turn 30. Spotrac estimates Bubic has a shot to land a four-year, $70 million deal, though he could easily make more than that figure if the his market remains popular. Will the Dodgers Re-Sign Kris Bubic? Bubic is a solid addition to most MLB rosters, but his likelihood of returning to Los Angeles isn’t high. Bubic would likely want to return to an MLB rotation rather than the bullpen, and he will earn more money doing so as well. The Dodgers’ rotation is stacked with talent, making a middling starter signing like Bubic unlikely. Would you bring Kris Bubic back to the Dodgers?

nigeria.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
nigeria.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday carried out the first-ever recovery of a spaceship, pulling off a successful “catch” of its Starship vessel as it returned to its launch site after a day in orbit. The spaceship emerged from a cloudy sky after withstanding the extreme heat of re-entering the Earth’s atmosphere, and descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The feat marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems — a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of space flight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into cheers as the spaceship eased into its high-tech nest on the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. This time the Starship spacecraft that gives the rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink satellite internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was extraordinarily complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters do. Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he added. ‘Giant swoosh’ The vessel’s path home was carefully mapped out by engineers. “If you want to get back to the east coast of Texas, you have to fly over the entire continent to get back there. So inevitably, you’re flying over land and we spend a lot of time figuring out the safest way to do that,” senior SpaceX engineer Lars Blackmore said. Starship flew over sparsely inhabited desert areas, wove over towns and then carried out a “giant swoosh maneuver” in its final approach, looping around the cities of Texas’ Rio Grande Valley and approaching its landing site from the east. Some versions of Starship are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while other iterations will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars. US space agency NASA is expecting Starship to serve as a lunar lander on its Artemis mission. On Saturday, Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated Musk and SpaceX. “It was almost magic… Making more believers by the day… one step closer to (the Moon),” he said on X. nigeria.title: Denmark hammer Ronaldo-less Portugal 4-1 in Nations League match
nigeria.description: Portugal were hammered 4-1 by Denmark on Saturday, an embarrassing Nations League defeat in their first match without Cristiano Ronaldo following the superstar forward’s retirement from international football. Rasmus Hojlund starred with a superb brace as Denmark moved into second place in Group A4 and closed in on a spot in the quarter-finals with a brilliant display in Braga. The Danes are on nine points from five fixtures, three behind Portugal who were already sure of qualification for the last eight having won all four of their previous group fixtures. A draw against third-placed Norway on Tuesday, 3-1 winners over Wales earlier, will see Denmark through. Ahead of kick-off Portugal paid tribute to Ronaldo, who announced his exit from the international game last week, with the team and mascots walking out wearing Ronaldo’s number seven and his name on their jerseys. Fans held up a huge banner which read “Thank you captain” as the teams entered the field, while applause rolled around the stadium once the match clock hit seven. Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to establish world records for goals and appearances in international football, netting 146 times in 234 matches. The highlight of his international career was winning Euro 2016, but it ended badly when the 41-year-old fell out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over not being selected for a Nations League fixture in September. That row led to the five-time Ballon d’Or winner being handed a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese football federation and his subsequent retirement, and Portugal looked liked they needed prime Ronaldo in a dismal display. Denmark were the better team from the first minute and it was no surprise when the away team went in at the break thanks to Pierre-Emile’s Hojbjerg’s spot-kick in the 43rd minute. Hojlund lashed home a brilliant volley four minutes after the restart and seven minutes later left the home crowd shellshocked with a strike of which Ronaldo would have been proud, the Napoli striker skipping past Ruben Dias before crashing home a powerful shot from the edge of the area. Boos and whistles began to ring out at the Estadio Municipal when Joachim Andersen headed in the fourth, and Bernardo Silva’s late consolation effort barely dampened the discontent. Antonio Nusa opened the scoring for Norway just before the hour mark in Oslo with a fine low strike before Andreas Schjelderup tapped home a perfect low cross from Erling Haaland, who rounded off the scoring from the penalty spot two minutes from time. Wales briefly had hope of getting a result when David Brook’s chipped finish halved the deficit in the 79th minute, but Craig Bellamy’s team will finish bottom of the group and risk being relegated to League B. He said himself, and the late Head of State Murtala Muhammad spearheaded the change in the country. Obasanjo said the youths have to be positively disruptive to bring about the desired change. “Most of the leaders of the immediate, pre and post-independent era were young and active. “They went for change, and they made it happen. Nigeria, as a whole, benefited from their activism. “Let me name two – Aminu Kano and Enahoro. The military era was not much different.” Earlier, the Vice Chancellor, Prof. Ajith Kumar, announced approval of new programmes by the National Universities Commission (NUC), adding that the university was the first in North-West Nigeria to receive approval for the B.Sc. Artificial Intelligence programme. He said the development further demonstrates its commitment to advancing technology-driven education in the region. Kumar said the institution has awarded a 50% scholarship to all toppers to pursue their postgraduate programmes at the university. Asekhauno told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday that the crash occurred at about 8.45 a.m. and involved a Sinotruck trailer, a Toyota Camry and a TVS commercial tricycle. She said that the vehicles had registration numbers AAA920YN, ENU622DR and NSH684VC, respectively. “Preliminary investigations indicated excessive speeding and inadequate construction warning signs as suspected factors responsible for the crash. “An eyewitness account indicated that the trailer, while descending a slope, noticed a diversion sign and attempted to manoeuvre into another lane. “The trailer reportedly collided sideways with the Toyota Camry, which subsequently hit the tricycle from behind, while the trailer somersaulted,” she said. The sector commander said that nine persons were involved in the crash, with one confirmed dead and eight sustained varying degrees of injuries. She added that five of the injured victims were taken to hospital for medical attention. According to her, the FRSC rescue team promptly mobilised to the scene to manage traffic and clear the obstruction. “The prompt intervention ensured the clearance and reopening of the blocked diversion route to motorists,” she said. Asekhauno expressed condolences to the family of the deceased and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery. She urged construction companies to provide adequate and visible warning signs, particularly around construction zones and diversion points, to guide motorists and prevent avoidable crashes. She also advised motorists to observe speed limits, exercise caution around diversions and construction areas as well as pay attention to road signs and traffic instructions. The sector commander reiterated FRSC’s commitment to prompt emergency response, effective traffic management and the protection of lives and property on Nigerian roads. nigeria.description: The Nigerian High Commission in South Africa has renewed its defence of newly accredited High Commissioner, Chief Femi Fani-Kayode, insisting that President Cyril Ramaphosa personally intervened in the controversy surrounding the presentation of his diplomatic credentials. That is a matter of concern to us,” the mission said. However, Magwenya disputed the Nigerian envoy’s account, prompting the Nigerian mission to insist that the South African President intervened to resolve the disagreement. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. sports.title: Arsène Wenger not expected to stand for FIFA presidency
sports.description: FILE PHOTO - FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development Arsene Wenger stands in the stadium prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League final soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid at Wembley Stadium. (is associated with: «Arsène Wenger not expected to stand for FIFA presidency») Robert Michael/dpa Arsène Wenger has decided against standing for the FIFA presidency in a boost for current incumbent Gianni Infantino, the Press Association understands. Wenger was touted as a potential rival to Infantino, who has lost the confidence of European football’s governing body, UEFA, over the controversial plan to seek private investment in a World Cup company. The deadline for candidates to declare their intention to stand is Wednesday, November 18, but former Arsenal manager Wenger has informed UEFA he will not go head-to-head with Infantino, the Press Association understands. It was first stated by UEFA in August that work to identify a credible candidate to challenge Infantino had got under way and Wenger was encouraged to stand. A senior figure in European football told the Press Association they believe Wenger would be the only person who could beat Infantino and put football first. Even though Wenger is European, he has served as FIFA’s chief of global football development since 2019 and has the respect of the football world after his Premier League success, which was preceded by successful stints in his homeland of France and Japan. Wenger had also earned a strong command of respect in Africa for his development work within FIFA but, in a blow to UEFA, the 77-year-old will not stand. This move could cement Infantino’s position as president despite the fallout of plans to create a company titled FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would manage commercial interests of FIFA’s competitions including the men’s and women’s World Cups. A private investor group, led by a company founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, were proposed to hold a minority stake in FFE. However, Infantino had to abandon the plan days after it emerged publicly after it was rejected by UEFA along with the Asian confederation and CONCACAF. It is the latest controversy regarding Infantino, who faced scrutiny after FIFA’s disciplinary committee decided to suspend a ban imposed on US forward Folarin Balogun during this year's tournament. Trump later admitted he had personally called Infantino to review Balogun’s suspension, but FIFA’s president has of late consolidated support as he targets a fourth term in position and Wenger’s decision to not stand is welcome news for the 56-year-old ahead of the FIFA Congress next March. Infantino has pledged “unanimous” backing from the Confederation of African Football (CAF), while the Asian confederation has U-turned and will now support his presidency bid.

sports.title: Why Marist football struggled in shut out by visiting Butler
sports.description: Marist struggled to move the ball consistently and turned it over twice as the Red Foxes slipped out of any contention for the Pioneer Football League title with a 28-0 loss to Butler before 2,167 at Tenney Stadium in Poughkeepsie on Saturday, Nov. 14. Gabe Passini capped an 11-play, 56-yard drive with a 1-yard TD run early in the fourth, and Desmin Jackson scored from 6 yards out 92 seconds later after Tristan Johnson picked off Mannino and returned it 42 yards. Marist was held to 52 total yards rushing and 141 passing. Isaiah Simmons had 10 carries for 36 yards. Lincoln Cardillo had five receptions for 32 yards, Reed Shumpert three for 48 and Zach Garmont three for 25. Kade Werner had nine tackles. sports.description: Declan Rice joined Ben White at Arsenal after signing from West Ham in 2023 [Getty Images] Declan Rice has defended Arsenal team-mate Ben White after the defender was booed at Wembley during England's 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday. White, who came on as a substitute in the Nations League fixture, left the Three Lions' camp at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar to return home for personal reasons. He then made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Gareth Southgate's reign. White was also booed by some fans in March's 1-1 draw with Ukraine after returning to the squad under Thomas Tuchel. "The incident with Ben was over five years ago, I don't know why it is still a conversation to be honest," Rice told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Knowing Ben, knowing the character he is, he has totally moved on from all of that. "He always wears the shirt with pride and every time he puts on the shirt, he gives 100 percent. "It shows his character. It is not easy being booed coming on at Wembley, but to show his mental strength to play the game and to play well, like he did in the previous months, is a real testament to him." Rice also said that the players do not discuss the situation at all and that everybody has moved on, adding that White has "an exciting future ahead with this England squad". Before the game, White said that people did not know the "full story" behind his departure from Qatar but that he still backed his decision. Rice close to signing new Arsenal contract Rice has also confirmed that he is close to signing a new contract with Arsenal. BBC Sport first revealed the midfielder was set to sign a new long-term deal at Emirates Stadium on 7 October, and the 27-year-old, speaking before England's game against Spain on Sunday, said: "A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon and I'm extremely lucky to be at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust and team-mates who put so much energy in to me." Rice's current deal expires in 2028 but the former West Ham star is now expected to extended his tenure in north London, having arrived from London Stadium in 2023 in a deal worth £105m. The midfielder's new contract will put him alongside Bukayo Saka as Arsenal's top earner. Rice has managed to avoid upheaval during his career and he believes that continuity has helped him to blossom. "I've been extremely lucky I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career. I always set myself targets, pushing for more," he said. sports.title: How did Minnesota survive travel adventure to Penn State football?
sports.description: STATE COLLEGE — This became a Penn State football day like no other. At least for visiting Minnesota Golden Gophers . How will the Gophers and Nittany Lions handle their travel and injury issues for their season-turning Big Ten game on Saturday, Nov. 14, in Beaver Stadium? Penn State will miss its star receiver Koby Howard for the seventh straight game to an undisclosed injury. He'll also be joined on the sideline by key backups, defensive end Caleb Bacon and cornerback Jahmir Joseph, both also listed as "out" on the Big Ten's pregame availability report . Nittany Lion starting left tackle Malachi Goodman and backup safety Jeremiah Cooper were listed as "game-time decisions" on the report. Minnesota was even a tougher personnel position: They are missing nine players for Saturday's game, including eight with starting experience. Of course, they're also dealing with an unprecedented travel adventure. Minnesota was one of the few in the Big Ten that got caught in the midst of Friday's four-hour nationwide travel ground stop by the Federal Aviation Authority. Their flight was canceled after the team had boarded in the afternoon. The Gophers, inexplicably, traveled back to campus and could not fly to State College until Saturday morning. They arrived barely seven hours before kickoff. Minnesota arrived carrying a lot of baggage even beyond their unusual same-day arrival. The Gophers and Penn State are both 5-4 but appear to be trending in different directions. While the Nittany Lions broke a four-game losing streak with back-to-back victories, the Gophers are coming off consecutive, excruciating defeats to top-five Indiana and UCLA − games they were tied or led in the fourth quarter. Minnesota owns one of the worst-rated offenses in the nation. They also are now missing their pair of starting defensive tackles, Riley Sunram and Theorin Randle and may be without standout defensive back John Nestor. Penn State's list of unavailable players for the Minnesota game includes Howard, Joseph, Bacon, linebacker Alex Tatsch, defensive ends Max Granville , offensive lineman Will Thompkins, cornerback Tyler Armstead and defensive tackle Alijah Carnell. sports.title: Dodgers All-Star Free Agent Commanding Widespread Interest
sports.description: Los Angeles Dodgers free agent Kris Bubic is gathering plenty of interest across MLB, per Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. The Dodgers acquired Bubic at the trade deadline on a rental, sending minor league reliever Carlos Duran the other way. “Free-agent left-hander Kris Bubic, who was traded from the Kansas City Royals to the Los Angeles Dodgers during his second stint on the injured list with elbow soreness, is drawing broad interest from contenders and non-contenders alike, according to a person briefed on his market,” Sammon and Rosenthal wrote. How Did Kris Bubic Perform With the Dodgers? Bubic came to the Dodgers on the injured list after struggling with elbow soreness, so he made just seven appearances out of the bullpen with the team throughout the regular season and postseason. Five of those appearances came in the regular season, where he held opponents scoreless through 4.2 innings pitched while striking out five batters. Bubic didn’t find the same success in the postseason, though, as he allowed two runs through 1.1 innings pitched. Sep 23, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers relief pitcher Kris Bubic (40) delivers against the San Diego Padres in the seventh inning at Dodger Stadium . Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Why is Kris Bubic Such a Popular Free Agent? Bubic, 29, is a starting pitcher by trade, but stepped into the bullpen for the Dodgers to manage his load after his injury. He has a versatile five-pitch arsenal, and he has a solid track record over the past few years despite a few injuries. Before an injury took him out of commission in July 2025, he had a 2.55 ERA through 20 starts and made the All-Star Game. This season, Bubic had a 3.76 mark through 14 appearances. Free agency is loaded with pitchers this offseason, with Tarik Skubal headlining a class which also consists of players like Freddy Peralta, Nick Martinez and Sonny Gray, but he is one of the top left-handed options available, and is one of the few still yet to turn 30. Spotrac estimates Bubic has a shot to land a four-year, $70 million deal, though he could easily make more than that figure if the his market remains popular. Will the Dodgers Re-Sign Kris Bubic? Bubic is a solid addition to most MLB rosters, but his likelihood of returning to Los Angeles isn’t high. Bubic would likely want to return to an MLB rotation rather than the bullpen, and he will earn more money doing so as well. sports.title: How San Antonio game vs. Baylor fits Sean Miller's quest for connection in Texas basketball
sports.description: Texas head coach Sean Miller watches his team warm up prior to an NCAA college basketball game against Grambling State in Austin, Texas, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. (AP Photo/Stephen Spillman) (Stephen Spillman/Associated Press) AUSTIN - From his corner office desk in one of the University of Texas' most impressive new buildings, Sean Miller can see what many of his predecessors couldn't. Campus, for one thing. In the old days, during the often successful and occasionally captivating eras of Abe Lemons, Tom Penders and Rick Barnes, the Longhorns men's basketball program was headquartered a few blocks away, on the other side of a rise that to most students might as well have been in San Marcos. The now-demolished Erwin Center served its purpose, but it always felt detached from the dormitories and the libraries and the massive stadium that, even more than the iconic school tower, represented what Texas money and know-how could achieve. Generations of basketball coaches tried to bridge that gap. It always proved to be more difficult than it appeared. But when Miller looks at the shrine to football just outside his office window, he eyes the potential for connection. "It's easy for me to embrace," the 57-year-old Miller says, leaning back on a sofa in the state-of-the-art basketball training facility next to the Moody Center, which opened in 2022. "Where I'm at in life, you really see things here that you know don't exist in other places." Other places have programs where the hoops culture is more deeply ingrained. Miller spent most of his life in places like that. He starred as a point guard in the Big East at Pittsburgh, cut his teeth as an assistant on Tobacco Road at North Carolina State, then won lots of games as a head coach throughout two stints at Xavier and one at Arizona. Texas, though, is a place where a basketball lifer like Miller finally can get over the top, and maybe even finish his career, if only he can find a way to channel its abundance of resources toward Final Fours. As a coach, he's never made one. As a program, the Longhorns haven't been to one in almost a quarter-century. To get there, Miller is trying to get the whole place on board. That means extending connections to the new football practice facility across the street, and to the swimming and diving program next door, and to donors in office buildings downtown, and even to chunks of the alumni base in cities like San Antonio. That's one reason why Miller decided to work with Baylor coach Scott Drew to bring Sunday's showdown between the former conference foes to Frost Bank Center. The Longhorns haven't played hoops in San Antonio since packing the Alamodome for an epic 2003 Elite Eight victory over Michigan State that sent them to their only Final Four of the past 79 years. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman . That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors. OpenAI has since restructured entirely . But it’s worth remembering what Helen and the board were supposed to do: OpenAI’s nonprofit board existed specifically to make sure the company didn’t betray its mission to build safe AI by prioritizing profit and growth over safety. science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever
science.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. While the double-catch attempt, and the chopsticks success with Ship, were Flight 15's main headlines, the mission had other objectives as well. One was getting Ship to orbit, which had happened on just one previous Starship launch — Flight 14 , which lifted off on Sept. 28. Ship deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) on Flight 14, and it did so again on Flight 15. These 52 spacecraft are the first members of a constellation that will eventually consist of 100,000 satellites , if all goes according to SpaceX's plan. Some of those Starlink satellites took video and images of Ship 42's heat shield to check its health for today's landing attempt. Those images, combined with ground-based cameras, found Ship 42 to be in good shape and ready for its big moment. SpaceX plans to use Starship to build an even bigger network in LEO than the Starlin

science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . science.title: New Scientist readers on how the magazine has shaped their lives
science.description: Have you been reading New Scientist since the start? Getty Images/Westend61 The first issue of New Scientist was published on 22 November 1956, and some of our readers have been with us since the very beginning. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Peter Hall Advertisement I seem to have been reading New Scientist for the full 70! I do recall my encounter with the first edition: I was at Bec Grammar School in south London in a second-year physics class – it was 1956. The teacher, a genial boffin-type, announced the advent of the new publication and handed out copies – all I remember is its grey (or was it beige?) pages, which I read in a perfunctory way (I was only 12!) little thinking it would follow me through life and around the globe. Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. I am very grateful to New Scientist for maintaining my interest in all the sciences and new developments, which I am sure has helped me to think laterally and to have a greater understanding of what makes everything tick. Frank Eva

science.title: SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)
science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Future/Josh Dinner, Space.com) Ship goes to orbit Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. All went according to plan after that for Ship as well: A second engine burn lasting about 20 seconds parked Ship in LEO at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) at T+26 minutes and 10 seconds. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." Ship first reached orbit on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28. Ship carried 26 of SpaceX's Starlink V3 spacecraft, which were deployed into LEO on schedule today over a 42-minute span starting 35 minutes after launch. The upgraded wireless internet satellites are the second V3 batch to reach orbit, after a set of 26 that were delivered on Flight 14 . V3s are significantly more powerful than SpaceX's V2 Starlinks, which currently number more than 11,000 in LEO. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. The most famous depiction of the 1833 Leonids, actually produced in 1888 for the Adventist book Bible Readings for the Home Circle . The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin, that is in turn based on a first-person account of the 1833 storm by a minister, Joseph Harvey Waggoner on his way from Florida to New Orleans. science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

In many of the biggest science fiction franchises, conversing with alien races is an absolute doddle. In " Star Trek ", universal translators come as standard, while C-3PO has spent the last 49 years reminding everyone in "Star Wars" that he's fluent in over six million forms of communication. But in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak. In fact, working out how to establish a dialogue with extraterrestrial visitors becomes the whole point of this powerful and heartbreaking story, as the fate of planet Earth hinges on the interpretation of a single noun. The film's journey to the big screen began when a screenwriter best known for his work on horror franchises such as "Final Destination", "A Nightmare on Elm Street" and "The Thing" read a short story in an online magazine. science.title: 100 launches! Rocket Lab sends Earth-observing satellite to orbit on milestone mission (photos)
science.description: null Rocket Lab just hit the century mark. An Electron rocket topped with a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite lifted off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site on Saturday (Nov. 14) at 12:30 a.m. EST (0530 GMT; 6:30 p.m. local New Zealand time). The mission, which Rocket Lab called "The Mountain God Rises," was a big one: It marked the 100th launch to date for the California-based company. The first stage of Rocket Lab's Electron rocket falls back to Earth during "The Mountain God Rises" mission on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) Rocket Lab launched for the first time in May 2017, sending the brand-new Electron up on a test flight from New Zealand. That effort failed, but Electron bounced back on its second-ever liftoff, delivering several cubesats to low Earth orbit (LEO) in January 2018. In the years since, the 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron has become one of the most prolific and reliable rockets in the world, carrying small payloads to the final frontier for a variety of customers. And it hit the century mark on Saturday in record-breaking fashion: No commercially developed rocket has gotten there faster, not even SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9 , according to Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck. "It's an unprecedented milestone for a commercial small-lift orbital rocket, and a threshold rarely crossed in modern spaceflight," Beck said on Monday (Nov. 9), during Rocket Lab's third-quarter earnings call with investors. "But what matters most to us and our customers is that we have achieved a 96% reliability rate across 99 launches." Electron met the moment in style on Saturday morning, thanks to some fancy livery. "Black rocket 🤝 Golden milestone. Electron is all dressed up for launch 100," Rocket Lab said via X on Tuesday (Nov. 10), in a post that shared a photo of the specially painted first stage. Not all of Rocket Lab's missions have gone orbital, it should be noted: A suborbital variant of Electron known as HASTE , which customers use to test technologies in a hypersonic flight environment, has nine missions under its belt to date. The Electron rocket that flew Rocket Lab's 100th mission sported some special livery. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) "The Mountain God Rises" was Rocket Lab's 11th launch to date for the Tokyo-based company iQPS, which is building a constellation of three dozen synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites in LEO. And all went to plan on the mission: Electron's upper "kick stage" deployed a single iQPS spacecraft 357 miles (575 kilometers) above Earth. SAR satellites can see through cloud cover and image our planet at night as well as during the day, offering key advantages over spacecraft that are optimized to view in optical wavelengths.
